classification.difficultyReason: Read intersections and parallel marks, then recognise that AC and CB name the same complete line, so their common labelled points are A, B and C.

content.prompt: Look at the third diagram to the right.

spec.sourceRegion: Exercise 6A question 3, third diagram on the right
spec.description: Four extended lines concur at X. A lies below X on a steep line, B below-right on a descending line, C to the right on a shallow descending line, and Y above-right on a rising line. A, B and C lie in order on a second rising line. Matching single arrow marks identify AC and XY as parallel. Ordinary source blue strokes are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: AX, BX, CX and YX are concurrent at X; A, B and C are collinear; AC is parallel to XY.
spec.answerVisibility: All lines, labels and parallel marks are permanent question givens; no answers are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Name the four concurrent lines passing through the point $X$.

answer.worked: The four lines through $X$ also pass through $A$, $B$, $C$ and $Y$, respectively. They are $AX$, $BX$, $CX$ and $YX$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Name the two parallel lines, using the correct symbol for ‘is parallel to’.

answer.worked: The matching arrow marks show that $AC\parallel XY$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Name the intersection of the lines $BX$ and $AC$.

answer.worked: $B$ lies on both $BX$ and $AC$, so their intersection is $B$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Name the line joining $C$ and the intersection of $AX$ and $BX$.

answer.worked: $AX$ and $BX$ intersect at $X$. The line joining $C$ to $X$ is $CX$.

children.label: e
children.prompt: What points belong to both lines $AC$ and $CB$?

answer.worked: $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear, so $AC$ and $CB$ name the same line. All three labelled points belong to both lines.

children.label: f
children.prompt: What points belong to both lines $AC$ and $XY$?

answer.short: None; the two lines are parallel.
answer.worked: $AC\parallel XY$. Parallel lines have no point in common, so no points belong to both lines.
